title: Adding Lucene-style ?q= query string search for alerts made the Postgres backend build WHERE clauses by str.format()-ing user search terms into SQL.

agent_errors.message: SQL injection review returned no parsable findings for tests/test_queryparser.py lines 26-200

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The new SearchTerm.to_sql builds SQL by interpolating attacker-controlled identifiers directly into the SQL text via f-strings, with no allowlist. self.tokens.field[0] (the field name from the ?q= query, e.g. `foo:bar`) is embedded as a quoted identifier in lines like `f'"{self.tokens.field[0]}" ILIKE %({p})s'` and `f'"{self.tokens.field[0]}" ~* %({p})s'`. self.tokens.attr (from `attr.fieldname`)

findings.explanation: The new SearchTerm.to_sql builds SQL by interpolating attacker-controlled identifiers directly into the SQL text via f-strings, with no allowlist. self.tokens.field[0] (the field name from the ?q= query, e.g. `foo:bar`) is embedded as a quoted identifier in lines like `f'"{self.tokens.field[0]}" ILIKE %({p})s'` and `f'"{self.tokens.field[0]}" ~* %({p})s'`. self.tokens.attr (from `attr.fieldname`) is embedded as `f'"{tokens_attr}"::jsonb ->>...'` after only a `.replace('_','attributes')` transform, and self.tokens.fieldname is embedded in the subquery branch as `f'"{self.tokens.fieldname or self.tokens.field[0]}"'`. These identifiers are not bound parameters (only the values are bound via %({p})s), so a crafted field/attr name containing a double-quote can break out of the identifier and inject arbitrary SQL. The resulting SQL is executed in base.py via `WHERE {query.where}` with the bound vars, so the injected identifier text runs unparameterized.

findings.suggested_fix: Validate field/attr/fieldname identifiers against a strict allowlist of known column and attribute names (or a safe identifier regex) before interpolating them into SQL, and reject any value containing quotes or non-identifier characters. Never build SQL identifiers from raw user input; only values should be passed as bound parameters.
